text: Understanding Git branching is essential for modern software development. A branch lets you work on new features without affecting the main code. Developers often create feature branches to build and test their changes safely. When the work is ready, they merge the branch back into the main one. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the code. This version control workflow keeps projects organized and reduces mistakes. By using branches, merging, and pull requests together, teams can collaborate smoothly and maintain a stable, reliable codebase.
